request.spec:
Add a summary panel to the screen. Per grade: the count of people on that grade today (retired
people excluded) and their due-totals added up. Per period: its due-total. Per status: the count
of claims with that status. Every figure must agree with the list.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Add a summary panel to the screen. Per grade: the count of people on that grade today (retired
people excluded) and their due-totals added up. Per period: its due-total. Per status: the count
of claims with that status. Every figure must agree with the list.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the summary panel and all 4 acceptance tests pass on `bin/e2e`.

The panel is worked out in the browser from the data the screen already loads, so there are no server or database changes. To keep its figures in step with the list, it uses the same calculations the list does:

- **Per grade (A, B, C):** it counts the people who aren't retired and have that grade on the sheet's today. Their due-totals are added up with the same `personDue` the people list uses, skipping "n/a".
- **Per period:** I moved the period due-total calculation out of the Periods panel into a shared `periodDue` in `features/periods/periods.ts`. The Periods table and the summary now both use it, so the two figures can't differ. For a closed period it's still the total fixed when it was closed.
- **Per status (DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED, VOID):** it counts every claim on the sheet with that status, including retired people's claims. The test expects this: in its first scenario the SETTLED and VOID counts come only from Cam, who has retired.

The app has no PENDING status anywhere, so that count is always 0. I show it only because the test expects a `summary-status-PENDING-count` element.

The panel is in the new file `features/summary/summary.slot.tsx`, and it sits after the sheet totals on the screen.
